c4isr_products.name: ARTEMIS (Airborne Reconnaissance and Targeting Exploitation Multi-Mission Intelligence System)
c4isr_products.description: Contractor-owned, contractor-operated (COCO) airborne ISR service on a modified Bombardier Challenger 650. Leidos supplies aircraft, mission systems, flight ops and support; the Army pays by flight hour and connects to the sensors remotely via SATCOM. Operating in the EUCOM AOR; extended through summer 2027 plus two option years (FACT; Leidos release 2026).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: airborne multi-INT sensor collection (SIGINT/radar class payloads; exact payloads not public). Process: onboard collection, SATCOM backhaul to remote operators. Output: ISR products/feeds to Army theater intelligence consumers. Users: Army INSCOM / EUCOM aerial ISR units.

c4isr_products.name: Common Hardware Systems-6 (CHS-6) - C5ISR hardware procurement vehicle
c4isr_products.description: Single-award Army IDIQ (max $7.9B, 4-year base + two 3-year options, awarded Sept 2023) through which the Army buys ruggedized COTS command, control, communications, computers, cyber, ISR hardware; also used as the ordering vehicle for the 2026 ARTEMIS extension (FACT).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: Army unit/program hardware requirements. Process: catalog engineering, integration, logistics, refresh. Output: fielded tactical computing/network hardware. Users: Army tactical units and PEO C3N programs.

c4isr_products.name: Defense Enclave Services (DES) / DoDNet
c4isr_products.description: DISA single-award IDIQ ($11.5B ceiling, 10 years, awarded Feb 2022) consolidating Fourth Estate agency networks onto a common enterprise network; Leidos has run DoDNet operations since Feb 2022 (FACT per Leidos and Inside Defense; ceiling is NOT revenue).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: legacy agency networks/users. Process: migration, network operations, security, service desk. Output: a common DoD enterprise network for Fourth Estate agencies. Users: DISA and ~22 defense agencies/field activities.

c4isr_products.name: NGEN-R SMIT (Navy Next Generation Enterprise Network - Service Management, Integration and Transport)
c4isr_products.description: Navy enterprise network (NMCI/ONE-Net) services contract, up to $7.7B, won 2020 (FACT). A $926M Navy award reported in 2026 alongside the ARTEMIS award is, by headline, an NGEN-related award; details not fetched (INFERENCE from headline; MEDIUM).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: Navy/USMC enterprise users. Process: network transport, service management, integration. Output: operated enterprise network. Users: Navy and Marine Corps shore users.

c4isr_products.name: Dynetics air defense and autonomy products (Enduring Shield launcher; Sea Hunter/Seahawk USVs)
c4isr_products.description: Subsidiary Dynetics builds the Army IFPC Inc 2 'Enduring Shield' launcher (integrates with IBCS) and Leidos built the DARPA/Navy Sea Hunter and Seahawk medium USVs (RECALL - not re-verified this session; MEDIUM).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: fire-control/IBCS tracks (Enduring Shield) or mission plans (USV). Output: engagements or autonomous maritime ISR patrols. Users: Army air defense units; Navy unmanned task forces.

companies.exact_problem_solved: Runs very large enterprise/tactical networks and hardware supply chains at scale (DES, NGEN, CHS-6) and delivers ISR aircraft as a per-hour service (ARTEMIS) so the Army/Navy/DISA can field capability without owning platforms or staff. In C4ISR terms it is a transport/hardware/operations prime rather than a C2 software product company.
primary_users: DISA and Fourth Estate agency users
Army tactical units buying C5ISR hardware
primary_buyers: Army Rapid Capabilities and Critical Technologies Office / IFPC (Dynetics)
companies.hw_sw_mix: both - services-heavy prime; hardware integrator/reseller under CHS-6; ISR aircraft platform provider; limited standalone C2 software products.
companies.market_posture: defense-native (with civil, health and commercial segments)
